present_on_scene_date.note: Same problem as McKee's: the establishment list is not dated to 1835 and the treaty obligation behind the post had been superseded.

persons.name: Joseph Porthier

occupation.note: Striker to the government blacksmith at the Indian agency - the man who swings the sledge for the smith. Andreas names him in the agency establishment under Owen: 'David McKee as blacksmith, and Joseph Porthier as striker'. The occupation vocabulary has no separate entry for a striker and blacksmith is the trade he was in.

persons.note: A WAGE-EARNING ASSISTANT, WHICH THIS DATASET HAS ALMOST NONE OF, and a member of a family the 1833 treaty names: the schedule of payments in lieu of reservations carries 'Victoire Porthier and her children, $700'. Andreas's chapter on the early settlement treats the Mirandeau and Porthier families together as part of the French and mixed-descent community at Chicago.

research_note: THE ONLY DOCUMENTED STRIKER IN THE DATASET, and a reminder of how the documented population is skewed. Andreas names hundreds of proprietors and perhaps a dozen employees; this man is in the record only because the agency's payroll was a matter of federal accounting. STANDING CONSTRAINT. AGENTS.md: the final removal of the Potawatomi from Chicago occurred in August 1835, inside this project's first target year and six weeks AFTER the scene date; Native presence, representation and depiction are not research gaps to be filled by inference, and v1 ships no human figures at all. This record is a dataset entry that states what named sources say about a named person and adds nothing. It carries review_required so that no scene containing it can be marked released before the consultation the project has committed to.
